title: ModaLens: Measuring Image Sensitivity in Report-Conditioned Medical VLMs

cost.compute_notes: PDF (45 pp) fetched with `curl -sL -o modalens.pdf https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.15635v1`; main text (Secs 1-6) read in full via pdftotext; appendices A-N not read. Code repository advertised in the abstract returned 404 (with an invented-name control also 404, and the repo absent from the org's public list), so nothing could be run.

claims.statement: With the radiology report in the prompt, swapping the image for another study's changes MedGemma-27B's generated answer on 4.26% of trials; without the report on 20.94%, a paired increase of 16.7 points (patient-clustered 95% CI [15.6, 17.7]).
claims.scope: MIMIC-CXR test split, 3,199 cases from 293 patients, 14 questions per case (44,786 paired trials), explicit Yes/No answer instruction, image first. Under the original prompt with a lowercase first-token readout: 4.70% vs 17.07%, +12.4 [11.2, 13.6]. One institution, frontal films, English reports.

quantities.name: report_effect_on_flip_rate_points
quantities.baseline: absent minus present, patient-clustered bootstrap over 293 patients

our_assessment.why: Direction is robust across readouts, templates, option order, an Uncertain option, three model lineages and substitute redraws, per the authors. Magnitude is not: block order alone moves the report effect from +12.4 to +7.8 on identical trials, and the pooled rate is a mix of findings at ceiling (five findings answer yes on 97.8-100% of report-absent trials) and findings that flip 16.8-32%. Quote the direction and the range, not '16.7 points' alone.

claims.statement: Removing the report does not reveal competent image reading: on the label-conditioned one-question set no tested model (MedGemma, Qwen3.5 9B/27B, LLaVA-NeXT) reads the substituted image above chance, so what replicates across lineages is report anchoring, not image competence.
claims.scope: Secondary one-question design; on the all-14 unit MedGemma's image does carry signal (image adds 0.165 balanced accuracy without the report).

our_assessment.why: The authors state the circularity themselves: labels are report-derived, so 'adding the image lowers accuracy' means 'moves away from the report's label', not 'the image misleads'. This is the correct reading and the paper holds to it.

claims.statement: Warning the model that the report may not describe the image and may be wrong leaves report anchoring intact: one-question flip rate 1.50% under the warning vs 1.22% plain, +0.28 points [-0.13, 0.74]; under the warning the readout matches the substituted image's label on only 8.49% of label-changed pairs.
claims.scope: Framing intervention only, no temporal consistency enforced.

our_assessment.why: A prompt warning is not a control on modality reliance. Useful negative result for anyone who thinks 'tell it to look' is a fix.

claims.statement: Answer-bearing text drives the reduced sensitivity: length-matched neutral prose gives an 8.2% flip rate and boilerplate 7.1% (vs 10.3% no report, 1.4% full report); deleting the sentences that mention the queried finding raises it to 11.6%; a sentence stating the answer lowers it to 3.1%.
claims.scope: One-question design, text-content controls; the authors note these do not fully isolate content from length and context.

our_assessment.why: The right negative controls. Note neutral prose alone lowers sensitivity from 10.3% to 8.2%: part of the 'report effect' is any-text-present, not report content.

claims.statement: A cumulative attention block on report-token positions restores image-swap sensitivity when it begins at or below about layer 22 of 62 and not from layer 28 upward (flip rate 1.50% to 7.75% when blocked from layer 0, against 12.00% with no report); difference-of-means steering and a linear probe transfer are negative.
claims.scope: 400 one-question cases; report-specific against controls only over layers 0-20. A bound on when direct access to report tokens matters, explicitly not a localisation of report use.

our_assessment.why: Carefully bounded by the authors; the negative steering and probe results are reported with the same care as positives, which is rare.

relations.why: ModaLens measures a near-100% report-absent yes rate for support devices in MedGemma. If the benchmaxxing model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) shares such a prior, '143 of 150 correct alone' is a prior, not a reading.
relations.asymmetric_note: Different models. This raises a hypothesis about the benchmaxxing arm and does not confirm it; the benchmaxxing adoption rate is untouched.

open_questions: The code repository is advertised and 404 on 2026-09-30. Re-check; if it becomes public, the run records make most numbers here re-checkable without PhysioNet access.
The report effect halves with text-first block order. Is there any order-independent summary of modality reliance, or is 'flip rate' inherently a property of the prompt as well as the model?

Report-derived labels cannot score visual correctness. The classifier surrogate (TorchXRayVision) is the only image-level label. What is the smallest radiologist-annotated subset that would turn this sensitivity audit into a correctness audit?

For the Dojo CosmosReason2 ticket: the paired image-swap audit is a cheap, report-free test of whether a general VLM uses the image at all on medical inputs (VQA-RAD image-decisive questions: 61.5% flip for MedGemma).
